metadata.question: Was there more sea ice visible in Hudson Bay (56.271030, -87.160422) on July 29, 2020 than on July 13, 2020?

data.raw_code: The user is asking about sea ice visibility in Hudson Bay on two specific dates: July 29, 2020 vs July 13, 2020. Key considerations: 1. Data source: Need satellite imagery that can detect sea ice. Sentinel-2 or Landsat would work. 2. Sea ice detection: Can use NDVI or simple reflectance thresholds since ice has high reflectance. 3. Location: Hudson Bay at (56.271030, -87.160422) - should create a point or small buffer around it. 4. Dates: Very specific - July 29, 2020 and July 13, 2020. 5. Comparison: Need to quantify "more sea ice" - likely pixel count of ice vs water. Approach: - Use Sentinel-2 for better temporal resolution - Create a small buffer around the point - Use NDVI or simple reflectance to classify ice vs water - Compare pixel counts between the two dates - Handle potential cloud cover with cloud masking Potential issues: - Cloud cover on either date could lead to C1 or C2 - Need to validate that the detection method works for sea ice ```javascript const ee = require('@google/earthengine'); const privateKey = require('../auth_keys/test-project-473922-29f05d49bed7'); async function runAnalysis() { // 1. Geometry & Time Definitions const point = ee.Geometry.Point([-87.160422, 56.271030]); const region = point.buffer(5000); // 5km buffer around point const date1 = '2020-07-13'; const date2 = '2020-07-29'; // 2. Data Acquisition - Sentinel-2 for sea ice detection function getCollection(date) { return ee.ImageCollection('COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED') .filterBounds(region) .filterDate(date, ee.Date(date).advance(1, 'day')) .filter(ee.Filter.lt('CLOUDY_PIXEL_PERCENTAGE', 80)); } const col1 = getCollection(date1); const col2 = getCollection(date2); // Check collection sizes const size1 = col1.size().getInfo(); const size2 = col2.size().getInfo(); console.log(`July 13 Images: ${size1}, July 29 Images: ${size2}`); if (size1 === 0 || size2 === 0) { console.log("C1"); return; } // Get least cloudy image for each date const img1 = col1.sort('CLOUDY_PIXEL_PERCENTAGE').first(); const img2 = col2.sort('CLOUDY_PIXEL_PERCENTAGE').first(); // 3. Sea ice detection using reflectance - ice has high reflectance in blue/green bands function detectSeaIce(img) { // Use blue band (B2) for ice detection - ice has high reflectance const blue = img.select('B2'); // Simple threshold: values > 2000 likely indicate ice/snow const iceMask = blue.gt(2000); return iceMask.rename('ice'); } const ice1 = detectSeaIce(img1); const ice2 = detectSeaIce(img2); // 4. Count ice pixels const count1 = ice1.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.sum(), geometry: region, scale: 100, maxPixels: 1e9 }).get('ice').getInfo(); const count2 = ice2.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.sum(), geometry: region, scale: 100, maxPixels: 1e9 }).get('ice').getInfo(); console.log(`July 13 ice pixels: ${Math.round(count1)}, July 29 ice pixels: ${Math.round(count2)}`); // Check for valid pixels if (count1 === null || count2 === null || isNaN(count1) || isNaN(count2)) { console.log("C3"); return; } if (count1 === 0 && count2 === 0) { console.log("C2"); return; } // 5. Final comparison if (count2 > count1) { console.log("A"); } else { console.log("B"); } } async function initEE() { await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.data.authenticateViaPrivateKey(privateKey, resolve, reject); }); await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.initialize(null, null, resolve, reject); }); await runAnalysis(); } initEE(); ```
